node_definition.done_when: derive_schedule in reckon/schedule.py gives each bar a state: recorded for a terminal status; in flight when a run whose phase is working, starting or dispatched serves the plan; held when its effective status is blocked or its only runs are held; predicted otherwise; pointers in other phases set neither state nor position. Every bar that is not recorded has an anchor (now, or the latest prerequisite's end when later); its remaining share runs from the anchor for (1-p)*w and its done share sits behind it for p*w, p being the plan's progress and w its wall-clock hours; a recorded bar ends at its landing as today; each bar carries its split point. Each bar carries its plan's typed key (nav_key from reckon/resources.py) and its lane index from the server's packing, and the schedule report (reckon/roadmap.py) names the lane count. docs/ui/crew.jsx draws the served state, position, split and lane, shading the done share, resolving each bar to its inventory row by its typed key and never by bare slug, with no status-to-state mapping, run lookup or lane packing of its own; rows are labelled as lanes, live only from a served in-flight bar. tests/test_the_flow_draws_each_plan_where_its_progress_puts_it.py derives the schedule for a temporary project at a fixed reference instant and asserts: a 50% plan of 18 hours with no live run spans -9 to +9, split at 0; a 100% plan that is not recorded ends at now; a plan served by a working run is in flight at the same position, and an older held pointer moves neither its state nor its start; an in-progress plan whose effective status is blocked is held; a draft plan with a working run is in flight; where a plan and a research document share a slug the bar carries the plan's typed key; every bar carries a lane index and no two bars in one lane overlap. Its negative control restores full-length placement from the reference instant, and the 50% assertion fails. A test in the style of tests/test_spa_derived_flow.py renders a served payload and asserts each bar's state class, position and lane come from the payload, and that where a plan and a research document share a slug the drawn bar shows the plan's sprint and progress, not the research row's. tests/test_spa_derived_flow.py, tests/test_schedule_derivation.py, tests/test_served_schedule_payload.py and tests/test_every_surface_shows_the_one_progress_figure.py are updated to the new contract without deleting or loosening any case. Tests importing reckon/schedule.py or reckon/roadmap.py, and the SPA test files, show no added failure against base (the coordinator runs the full population at merge); browser tests must run, not skip. Every log sits under the run directory and ends in EXIT=, suites run on the fleet allocation and not the login node, and ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the changed Python files.
